Conversation, family & daily routines · Time, the calendar & feasts

last night phrase

also the night before last

classical

Traupman 87–89

proximā nocte

Other words

  • hāc nocte — tonight, last night

    also used · classical · Traupman 87–89

  • heri vesperī — last night, yesterday evening

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 11.1.1: heri vesperī apud mē Hirtius fuit (Lewis & Short s.v. heri); Traupman 35

    Of the evening before, up to bedtime; of the night itself, proximā nocte. Heri has a short final i (see yesterday evening).

  • superiōre nocte — the night before last

    also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.1: quid proximā, quid superiōre nocte ēgerīs; Traupman 88

    With proximā nocte beside it, “the night before”. Proxima nox is the nearest night, so in a future context it is the coming night: proximā nocte, on the following night (Traupman 88).

Examples

  • quid proximā, quid superiōre nocte ēgerīs

    what you did last night, and what the night beforeCic. Cat. 1.1

See also tonight, yesterday evening.
